issues.issue: All three webhook handlers call `req.platform!.requestId` in every log statement, and `inventory_levels/update` passes `req.platform!` to `shopifyClientFor(req.platform!)`, but the platform contract explicitly states `req.platform` is NOT set on webhook routes (they are HMAC-identified, not verify-platform middleware paths).
issues.failure_mode: Every webhook delivery that reaches any log statement throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'requestId')` and crashes the handler before completing; `inventory_levels/update` also crashes at the Shopify API resolution step for uncached inventory items — all inventory availability transitions, variant-deletion health updates, and purchase-record writes silently fail on every delivery.

issues.issue: After `bridge.pickResource` returns variant picks, the code stores `p.id` (a Shopify GID string such as `'gid://shopify/ProductVariant/12345'`) as both `variantExternalId` and `productExternalId`; these GID strings are then sent verbatim as `variant_external_ids` and `product_external_ids` to `/bundles/items/save`, where the backend does `variantExternalIds.map(Number)` producing `NaN` for every entry before passing the array into the `::bigint[]` cast.
issues.failure_mode: PostgreSQL rejects `NaN` cast to `bigint`, throwing a DB error on every attempt to save bundle items from the admin editor; merchants receive a 500 and can never persist variant selections to any bundle — the core bundle-setup flow is completely broken.

issues.issue: `fmtMoneyAs` unconditionally divides `order_total_minor_units` by 100 (`(minor || 0) / 100`), and the CSV export does the same (`r.order_total_minor_units / 100`), ignoring that zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW) have a multiplier of 1 and three-decimal currencies (BHD, JOD) have a multiplier of 1000.
issues.failure_mode: A JPY order stored as `1500` minor units (= ¥1500) is displayed as ¥15.00 — a 100× understatement; a BHD order stored as `1500` minor units (= 1.500 BHD) is displayed as 15.00 BHD — a 10× overstatement; merchants in affected locales see systematically wrong order totals in the purchase-history table and in exported CSV files.
